name: Builders at the edge of Web3, quant finance & NLP
address: 31/F, The Centrium, 60 Wyndham Street, Central, Hong Kong
coverAlt: HKML Season 7 Episode 5 attendees in conversation at Bullish
excerpt: A year-end evening bringing together builders from Web3, quantitative finance, and natural language processing.
introduction: Our final meetup of the year explored how machine learning continues to reshape industries in very different ways—from market infrastructure to language systems. Three focused talks, candid questions, and an open networking session made space for both technical depth and new connections.

speakers.name: Dr. Maya Chen
speakers.talkTitle: Learning signals in digital asset markets
speakers.summary: A practical look at separating repeatable information from noise in always-on markets, with lessons from production research workflows.
speakers.bio: Maya leads quantitative research for an Asia-based digital assets team and works across market microstructure, statistics, and machine learning.

speakers.name: Aaron Leung
speakers.summary: How constrained language models can outperform larger alternatives when evaluation, latency, and domain context are designed together.
speakers.bio: Aaron builds applied NLP products and helps teams move language-model prototypes into reliable production services.

speakers.name: Priya Raman
speakers.summary: Design patterns for observable, reviewable agent workflows in high-consequence operational environments.
speakers.bio: Priya is a product engineering leader working at the intersection of AI systems, risk, and financial infrastructure.

name: Hedge funds’ reaching for beta & Asia frontiers
venue: HKU iCube by HKU Business School
address: Two Exchange Square, Central, Hong Kong
coverAlt: Audience attending an HKML event in Hong Kong
excerpt: Research and practice meet in an evening about monetary policy, hedge fund behaviour, and Asia’s market frontiers.
introduction: A collaborative HKML and HKDAS event connecting academic insight with real-world investment research.

speakers.name: Sofia Laurent
speakers.talkTitle: Monetary policy and hedge funds’ reaching for beta
speakers.summary: An empirical view of how shifts in monetary policy change risk taking and factor exposure among hedge funds.
speakers.bio: Sofia researches asset management, market structure, and the transmission of monetary policy.

speakers.name: Daniel Wong
speakers.talkTitle: Machine learning across Asia’s frontier markets
speakers.summary: What data availability, liquidity, and local market structure mean for applied ML research across Asia.
speakers.bio: Daniel is a systematic investor focused on Asian markets and alternative data.

name: Multi-agent RAG, climate signals & applied vision
coverAlt: Speaker line-up for HKML Season 7 Episode 2
excerpt: Three production-minded talks spanning fresh-data RAG, climate modelling, and practical computer vision.
introduction: This session focused on machine learning systems that work with imperfect, changing, real-world data.

speakers.name: Alex Hunsberger
speakers.summary: Learn from trial and error about answering natural-language questions by querying multiple data sources without stale data, using a multi-agent hierarchy within the RAG framework.
speakers.bio: Alex works on reliable information retrieval and agent systems for financial research.

speakers.name: Manish Raychaudhuri
speakers.talkTitle: Reading climate risk through alternative data
speakers.summary: A tour of modelling choices and validation challenges when physical and economic climate signals meet.
speakers.bio: Manish is a researcher and technology leader applying data science to complex investment questions.

speakers.name: Juncheng Li
speakers.summary: How robust representation choices change the outcome of vision systems deployed outside the lab.
speakers.bio: Juncheng’s research focuses on practical and trustworthy computer vision.

name: Teaching machines to hear the unsaid
excerpt: An evening on extracting tone from speech embeddings and building better models for human communication.
introduction: Season seven opened with a close look at what speech conveys beyond words—and how careful evaluation turns embeddings into useful signals.

speakers.name: Natalie Lau
speakers.talkTitle: Teaching machines to hear the unsaid
speakers.summary: Extracting tone from speech embeddings, with practical notes on data collection, representation, and evaluation.
speakers.bio: Natalie is a machine-learning researcher working on speech, language, and human-centred AI.

name: Responsible AI in the generative era
coverAlt: HKML audience at the AWS GenAI pop-up
excerpt: A grounded conversation about evaluation, governance, and responsibility in generative-AI products.
introduction: Researchers and practitioners shared concrete ways to make generative systems safer, more measurable, and easier to govern.

speakers.name: Amelia Ho
speakers.talkTitle: Responsible AI in the era of generative AI
speakers.summary: A field guide to moving from broad principles to measurable checks across a generative system’s lifecycle.
speakers.bio: Amelia advises product and engineering teams on trustworthy AI and model governance.

speakers.name: Marco Ng
speakers.talkTitle: Evaluations that survive contact with users
speakers.summary: Combining offline test sets, human review, and production monitoring to understand real system behaviour.

name: From ML research to resilient systems
excerpt: Lessons from taking promising research ideas into observable, dependable production systems.
introduction: A practical session about the decisions, trade-offs, and teamwork behind production machine-learning systems.

speakers.name: Chris Tam
speakers.summary: A compact set of patterns for turning experimental models into services that teams can understand and operate.
speakers.bio: Chris leads machine-learning engineering for a financial technology team.
